paragraphs.text: For a long time, forgetting was seen simply as a failure of memory. Psychologists now believe that it plays a useful role, allowing the brain to remove information that is no longer needed.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Early experiments showed that people forget most of a list of new words within a day unless they review them. Later studies found that spacing reviews over several days leads to much better long-term recall than repeating the list many times in one session.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Sleep also affects memory. Volunteers who slept after learning a set of facts remembered more of them the next morning than those who stayed awake, suggesting that the brain strengthens important memories during the night.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Stress can have the opposite effect. People who were asked to give a speech in front of strangers before a memory test recalled fewer words, although they remembered the stressful event itself very clearly.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Some researchers argue that forgetting details helps people to generalise. A child who forgets the exact appearance of every dog they have met may find it easier to recognise a new animal as a dog.
paragraphs.label: E
